article.title: There are significant amounts of microplastic in Sierra Nevada snow
article.summary:
University University of California, RiversideFor the first time, scientists have measured how much microplastic pollution falls on the Sierra Nevada during snowstorms and were surprised to find significant amounts even in the most remote locations.
As snowflakes fall, they collect some of these tiny plastic particles suspended in the air.
This process, called scavenging, helps explain why researchers measured substantially more plastic arriving with the falling snow than during dry weather.
At remote sampling locations, during the height of the storm, the snow deposited between 270 and 3,200 plastic particles per square meter, per day.
Researchers used infrared light to read chemical signatures, then compared those signatures with a reference library to distinguish plastic from soil and plant material.
